Criminal Revision No. 756 of 1978
With
Criminal Misc. No. 42 of 1979
lawyer:
A.B.M. Khairul Hoque, Advocate ------ For the petitioner
Mahfuzur Rahman Advocate ------ For the contemner
M.A. Baqui, Advocate ------ For the opposite party No. 2.
parties:
Abdul Aziz & Ors.
Vs.
The State & Ors.
full_judgment:
M.H. Rahman, J :—This application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is at the instances of the accused petitioners for quashing the criminal proceeding of Motijheel P.S. Case No. 41(S) 78 G.R. 6952/78 under sections 147/148/447 of the Bangladesh Penal Code now pending in the Court of Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar, South, Dhaka. 

 2. Opposite party No. 2 lodged a First Information Report before the Officer-in-charge, Motijheel Police Station, Dhaka on 17.8.78 alleging that he was a tenant under petitioner No. 1 in holding No. 14, Mugdapara and was running a business there and he was forcibly evicted from his but on 14.8.78, and on such allegations the Police recorded the above case. 

 3. On behalf of the petitioners it has been submitted that no such case could lie in view of the fact that the complainant had filed on 22.4.75 another criminal case, being Ramna P.S. Case No. 248(4) 75 under section 430/447/448 of the Penal Code, to the effect that he was forcibly removed from his but on 22.4.75. Opposite Party No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 239 of 1975 in the First Court of Munsif at Dhaka for permanent injunction making the same allegations as made in the criminal case. The Court passed an ad interim order of injunction which was made absolute on 24.2.78. The present petitioners preferred an appeal against that order and the learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka, set aside the order of temporary injunction after finding that the plaintiffs in that suit was not in possession of the suit land on the date of hearing of the temporary injunction. The learned Subordinate Judge passed the order on 30.5.78. In view of the aforesaid findings the petitioners have submitted that the institution of the criminal proceeding have been initiated by opposite party No. 2 only for causing harassment to the petitioners. 

 5. In view of the clear finding of the learned Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka in Misc. Appeal No. 122 of 1978 that the plaintiff was not in possession of the suit land on the date of hearing of the temporary injunction and in view of the earlier criminal case initiated by opposite party No. 2 alleging that he had been forcibly removed from the but in question on 22.4.75; we think there is substance in the contention of the petitioners and that if the present criminal proceeding is allowed to continue it will result in abuse of the process of Court. Accordingly, we make the Rule Absolute. The proceeding in Motijheel Police Station Case No. 41(9) 78 G.R. 6952/78 under section 147/148/447 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar South, Dhaka is hereby quashed. 

 6. Along with this Criminal Revision we have taken up Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 42 of 1979 where a Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and opposite party No. 1 Md. Khalilur Rahman, Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka Collectorate, Dhaka to show cause why opposite party No. I should not be committed for contempt of this Court and suitably punished. 

 7. In the application for drawing up of a proceeding for contempt of Court the petitioners have stated that they obtained a Rule in Criminal Case No. 756 of 1978 on 12.12.78 and this Court directed for stay of further proceeding of the Criminal Proceeding in question. On 13.12.78 the learned Advocate for the petitioners moved an application before the Sub-Divisional Officer, (South), Dhaka for staying of the criminal case contending, inter alia, that this Court had already issued a rule and stayed further proceedings of G.R. Case No. 6952 of 1978, and filed there the certified copy of the order of this Court. The Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar South, transferred the case along with the petition to the contemner. The learned Advocate for the petitioners renewed his prayer before Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, Magistrate, 1st Class, the contemner who after reading the certified copy of the order threatened to cancel the bail bond of the petitioners unless a fresh prayer for bail was made. On 15.1.79 the learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners filed another application for stay of further proceeding. The contemner neither rejected nor considered that petition and in total disregard of the order of this court directed issuance of warrant of arrest to the prosecution witnesses and fixed 15.2.79 for examination of the prosecution witnesses. 

 8. Mr. Mahfuzur Rahman, learned Advocate for the contemner has submitted that the contemner has taken away the brief from him long ago and he is now in custody in connection with a case under section 302 of the Penal Code. 

 10. Mr. Mahfuzur Rahman, learned Advocate for the contemner has submitted that he prepared the affidavit and got it sworn by the contemner but before he could produce it before the Court the brief was taken away by the contemner in connection with another criminal case. 

 12. However, in view of subsequent circumstances and that as he is already in custody in connection with criminal case we are not inclined to award any sentence on the contemner. The contemner is discharged with severe warning. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.
